business_problem: Foodics needed near-real-time analytics for tens of thousands of restaurant branches, but older systems struggled with reliability, code-heavy integration work, and the scale of daily reports and jobs.
solution_summary: Foodics runs its restaurant-insights backbone on Snowflake so point-of-sale, finance, customer, and inventory intelligence can operate from one platform. Departments use Snowflake Secure Data Sharing to exchange governed datasets in their own ecosystems while still aggregating them for deeper analysis, and separated storage and compute lets Foodics scale to millions of reports and jobs without inflating cost. Engineers embed Snowflake's custom ODBC driver into application flows so live data can be surfaced to customers without large rewrites, and more business logic can execute inside the platform instead of scattered code. The same foundation supports anomaly detection, loyalty analysis, and predictive AI use cases for restaurant operators. Because Snowflake stays reliable under heavy volume, Foodics can serve near-real-time operational insight to more than 39,000 branches while freeing engineers to focus on value-added work rather than pipeline maintenance.

data_flow: Point-of-sale, finance, customer, and inventory data land in Snowflake on AWS, where departments share curated datasets through Secure Data Sharing and applications pull live results through the custom ODBC driver. Analytics and AI on the same foundation then produce near-real-time reports and predictive insight for restaurant operators.
business_outcome: Foodics now analyzes 80% more data, runs 2 million daily reports and 3 million daily jobs for more than 39,000 customers, and cut analysis and reporting effort in half while delivering timelier restaurant insight.
